factCheckIssues.problem: The draft cites SPM IN as 'V.2, Nov 2024' and links to that PDF. V.2 (dated 15 Nov 2024) was superseded on 17 Jan 2025, so both the citation and the link point to an outdated version.
factCheckIssues.evidence: BRDR search results: the IN 'V. 2' document is dated 15 November 2024 with a supersession date of 17 Jan 2025, and the current IN page (brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/spm/current/IN) shows an issue date of 17 Jan 2025.
factCheckIssues.fix: Changed ref to 'IN (Introduction); current version issued 17 Jan 2025' and the url to the BRDR current-IN page. Kept the V.2 PDF in sources.

factCheckIssues.problem: 'The HKMA requires compliance with the minimum standards' overstates the IN module's wording.
factCheckIssues.evidence: IN states that the Manual sets out the minimum standards AIs are expected to attain in order to satisfy the requirements of the Banking Ordinance, together with best-practice recommendations.
factCheckIssues.fix: Restated the summary in line with the IN wording.

factCheckIssues.problem: The draft defines a deposit as a loan 'repayable on demand or on agreed terms'. That is not the statutory definition, which turns on the interest or premium element.
factCheckIssues.evidence: HKMA Guide to Authorization, Chapter 2: s.2 defines 'deposit' as a loan of money at interest, at no interest or at negative interest, or repayable at a premium or with other consideration in money or money's worth, subject to exclusions (e.g. certain debenture/prospectus-related loans and loans tied to providing property or services).
factCheckIssues.fix: Rewrote the definition to follow the statute. Also added the 'deposit' definition to the provisions[2] summary.

factCheckIssues.problem: Two claims could not be confirmed: commencement dates (1 Jan 2027 / 1 Jan 2028 / 1 Jan 2032) and that the Bills Committee completed clause-by-clause scrutiny on 18 Sept 2026 (or that the Bill was before a Bills Committee in Sept 2026). Searches found only the gazettal (5 June 2026) and the scheduled First/Second Reading on 17 June 2026, and no Bills Committee record.
factCheckIssues.evidence: Government press release, 5 June 2026 (info.gov.hk P2026060500217): gazettal, five areas of amendment, five-year DTC transition, amendments to the HKAB Ordinance and FIRO. LegCo agenda (via search): First and Second Reading at the 17 June 2026 meeting, with the debate adjourned. No source found for the commencement dates or for a September 2026 Bills Committee.
factCheckIssues.fix: Removed the unconfirmed dates and committee progress from the deepDive and the provision summary and moved them to 'uncertain'. Replaced the vague 'amends other banking legislation, including enforcement powers' with the five confirmed areas and the scheduled 17 June 2026 reading. Revised the counselNote and the last pitfall to match.

factCheckIssues.problem: The cited LegCo Bills Committee minutes URL (yr2026/.../bc0320260918.pdf) could not be verified, and the claim it supported has been removed.
factCheckIssues.evidence: Several searches for a Bills Committee on the Banking Legislation (Miscellaneous Amendments) Bill 2026 returned no record.
factCheckIssues.fix: Removed the URL from sources.

factCheckIssues.problem: The draft refers generically to 'the exemptions in s.3'. It also omitted the statutory presumption that the drafter had seen but could not place.
factCheckIssues.evidence: HKMA Guide to Authorization, Chapter 2 (via search): s.3(1) specifies categories of non-authorized persons not subject to s.12(1). Section 12(8) presumes a business of taking deposits where deposits are taken on at least 5 separate occasions within any 30 days, absent evidence to the contrary.
factCheckIssues.fix: Pinpointed s.3(1) and added the s.12(8) presumption, sourced to the HKMA Guide, with a note in 'uncertain' that it was not checked against e-Legislation.

factCheckIssues.problem: The draft said s.2 defines 'the tier-specific businesses', which is unsupported. Its paraphrase of the 'at call or notice' limb was also loose.
factCheckIssues.evidence: HKMA Guide to Authorization, Chapter 2: s.2 defines 'banking business' (accounts repayable on demand or within less than three months, or at call or notice of less than that period; paying or collecting customers' cheques) and 'deposit'.
factCheckIssues.fix: Restated the definitions, removed 'tier-specific businesses' and added the 'deposit' definition. Also fixed the 'banking business' glossary entry.

factCheckIssues.problem: 'A DTC must be a local subsidiary' misstates the requirement. The requirement is local incorporation. The draft also omitted the DTC minimum capital, which it listed as unconfirmed.
factCheckIssues.evidence: Search results (HKMA 2001 market-entry press release and three-tier summaries): minimum capital is HK$300m for licensed banks, HK$100m for RLBs and HK$25m for DTCs, and all DTCs must be incorporated in Hong Kong.
factCheckIssues.fix: Changed to 'a DTC must be locally incorporated', added HK$25 million and removed the DTC capital item from 'uncertain'.

factCheckIssues.problem: The draft presented internet 'targeting' as statutory text. It is the MA's policy, set out in a guideline under s.92(6), and applies to offshore internet material.
factCheckIssues.evidence: HKMA press release 24 May 2002, 'Issue of Guideline by the Monetary Authority in relation to Section 92(6) of the Banking Ordinance'. HKMA Guide Chapter 2 states that s.92 does not prohibit advertising of deposits placed outside Hong Kong but that such material must meet the Fifth Schedule disclosure requirements.
factCheckIssues.fix: Attributed the targeting test to the s.92(6) guideline (May 2002) and confined it to offshore internet material. Raised confidence to high.

factCheckIssues.problem: The specific targeting factors (language, currency, contact details, geo-targeting) were attributed to s.92 but not verified against the s.92(6) guideline.
factCheckIssues.evidence: No source reviewed lists the guideline's factors.
factCheckIssues.fix: Rephrased to refer to the factors in the s.92(6) guideline without listing unverified ones. Added an 'uncertain' item.

factCheckIssues.problem: 'Insurance business needs IA licensing' conflates insurer authorization with intermediary licensing. A bank's activity is distribution.
factCheckIssues.evidence: Under the Insurance Ordinance, the IA licenses insurance intermediaries (the bank's bancassurance role) and separately authorizes insurers.
factCheckIssues.fix: Changed to 'insurance distribution needs IA licensing'. Also dropped 'even for a bank' (the point is covered in provisions[7].counselNote).

factCheckIssues.problem: The exemption for representative offices was not pinpointed.
factCheckIssues.evidence: HKMA Guide to Authorization, Chapter 7 (via search): s.97(1A) lets a local representative office of an overseas bank use its name in immediate conjunction with 'representative office'. HKMA treats domain names and logos as within s.97(1)(a).
factCheckIssues.fix: Added the s.97(1A) pinpoint. The domain-name and logo point is confirmed.

factCheckIssues.location: overview; glossary 'three-tier banking system'; deepDive (new watch-list paragraph)

factCheckIssues.fix: Added 'currently' in the overview. Updated the glossary definition. Added a short watch-list paragraph: gazetted 5 June 2026, most provisions proposed to commence 1 January 2027 if enacted.
factCheckIssues.evidence: Government press release 5 Jun 2026; LegCo LS33/2026; JSM and Stephenson Harwood briefings. First Reading 17 Jun 2026; Bills Committee meetings July and September 2026.

factCheckIssues.problem: 'Existing licences were not affected' could not be verified.
factCheckIssues.fix: Replaced with the verified point that the 25 Oct 2024 guideline superseded the 2018 guideline and that the authorization test remains the Seventh Schedule.
factCheckIssues.evidence: HKMA digital banks page and the Timothy Loh note dated 25 Oct 2024. No source found on the effect on existing licences.

factCheckIssues.problem: 'No strong case' paraphrase. HKMA said it did not see any strong justification for new VB players at that juncture.
factCheckIssues.fix: Reworded to 'no strong justification for new licences at that time'.
factCheckIssues.evidence: HKMA press release 6 Aug 2024 (20240806-3) as quoted in search.

factCheckIssues.problem: Implied all SPM modules are statutory guidelines. Some, such as CG-5, are non-statutory guidance notes.
factCheckIssues.fix: Added 'others are non-statutory guidance notes'.
factCheckIssues.evidence: HKMA letter of 29 Jul 2021 issuing CG-5 'as a guidance note'.

factCheckIssues.problem: Some uncertain items have been resolved, and new open points have arisen.
factCheckIssues.fix: Removed the IT assessment timing item (now resolved, with a caveat). Added items on the effect of suspension on deposit-taking, the status of the 2026 Bill, and the two-tier treatment of capital floors. Revised the item on the February 2026 re-issues.
factCheckIssues.evidence: See the evidence for the items above.

factCheckIssues.problem: The summary said the 2025 revision 'reportedly folded in the December 2021 circular and addressed conflicts arising from external directorships'. This is unverified. The HKMA said the updates were primarily to align with international standards. The version number was missing.
factCheckIssues.fix: Set ref to 'CG-1 (V.4, 1 Aug 2025)'. Replaced the unverified claim with the HKMA's own description. Added the table-of-contents topics (appointment, fit and proper, commitment, succession). Raised confidence to high.
factCheckIssues.evidence: HKMA letter of 1 Aug 2025 (20250731-2-EN): revised CG-1 gazetted that day under s.7(3), with updates primarily to align with international standards. CG-1 cover: V.4, 01.08.2025.

factCheckIssues.problem: Did not say that CG-5 is a non-statutory guidance note, unlike CG-1, and omitted the focus of the 2021 revision.
factCheckIssues.fix: Described CG-5 as a guidance note and added the FSB misconduct-risk focus of the 2021 revision. Raised confidence to high.
factCheckIssues.evidence: HKMA letter of 29 Jul 2021 (20210729-1-EN): revised CG-5 issued as a guidance note, mainly reflecting FSB guidance on remuneration tools for misconduct risk. V.1 2010, V.2 2015.

factCheckIssues.problem: The draft said the HKMA expects persons in charge of 'core functions' to be drawn from CEs, alternates, s.72B managers or executive directors. This mis-states the circular, which defines 'management' and requires identification of the individuals principally responsible for regulated-activity businesses and functions.
factCheckIssues.fix: Rewrote the summary and deepDive to match the circular: management means CEs and ACEs, s.71 directors, s.72B managers and s.71C executive officers, and submission with an organisation chart was due by 16 April 2018. Added s.71C consent for executive officers.
factCheckIssues.evidence: HKMA circular and FAQ 16 Oct 2017 (20171016-1-EN) as quoted in search; Clifford Chance, A&O and Regulation Tomorrow summaries.

factCheckIssues.problem: The mechanism for supervisory conditions on an intermediate holding company was left uncertain, although it is documented. The 2026 Bill on direct holding company supervision was omitted.
factCheckIssues.fix: Added that the HKMA currently attaches conditions to the holding company's s.70 consent, and that the Banking Legislation (Miscellaneous Amendments) Bill 2026 would create direct powers over designated holding companies. Updated the uncertain list.
factCheckIssues.evidence: LegCo Brief B&M/2/1/33C (3 Jun 2026): the MA currently acts only indirectly, by attaching conditions to s.70 consent for a holding company to become controller. Bill gazetted 5 Jun 2026; new Part XIIIA on bank holding companies.

factCheckIssues.problem: Incomplete: omitted the 2001 amendment enabling the MA to impose conditions on existing controllers.
factCheckIssues.fix: Added this point. Kept medium confidence and flagged the exact s.70A scope in uncertain.
factCheckIssues.evidence: Banking (Amendment) Ordinance 2001 materials (ord032-01-e) as summarised in search.

factCheckIssues.problem: Omitted the link between the s.72B regime (introduced in 2001) and the Fourteenth Schedule list of businesses and functions.
factCheckIssues.fix: Added this with medium confidence and flagged the Fourteenth Schedule content in uncertain.
factCheckIssues.evidence: HKMA 2017 FAQ: AIs must notify appointments of managers for the businesses and functions listed in the Fourteenth Schedule. 2001 LegCo papers describe the new s.72B and Fourteenth Schedule.

factCheckIssues.problem: Omitted the MA's power to withdraw consent.
factCheckIssues.fix: Added that the MA may withdraw consent if no longer satisfied that the person is fit and proper.
factCheckIssues.evidence: 2005 LegCo paper (bc050524cb1-ls70): the MA may withdraw consent by notice, with at least 7 days' advance notice of the decision and reasons.

factCheckIssues.problem: The BELR commencement date and CR-G-9 version were listed as uncertain, but both can be confirmed. The notifiable-event consequence was omitted.
factCheckIssues.fix: Stated that BELR has been in force since 1 July 2019 and that breach of the rule 87 limits is a notifiable event. Raised confidence to high. Narrowed the uncertain item to whether CR-G-9 V.5 has replaced V.4 (effective 1 Jan 2025).
factCheckIssues.evidence: HKMA Exposure Limits page (BELR effective 1 July 2019; Cap. 155S). LegCo brief 2018ln220-223: Part XV repealed on BELR commencement. CR-G-9 guidance: rule 87 breach is notifiable under rule 7(2)(l). CR-G-9 V.4 effective 1 Jan 2025; V.5 dated 'xx.12.2025'.

factCheckIssues.problem: Imprecise reference to the December 2018 measures.
factCheckIssues.fix: Attributed the measures to a December 2018 circular. Confirmed self-assessment, focused reviews and culture dialogues.
factCheckIssues.evidence: HKMA circular 'Supervision for Bank Culture', December 2018 (20181219-2-EN), via search.

factCheckIssues.problem: The checklist did not reflect the December 2018 culture circular or the pending holding company regime.
factCheckIssues.fix: Changed 'circular' to 'circulars' and added an assessment of the 2026 Bill's holding company regime.
factCheckIssues.evidence: As above.

factCheckIssues.problem: The URL for the 19 Aug 2024 GenAI circular pointed to the 5 Nov 2019 big data/AI circular (docId 20191105-1-EN), not the 2024 circular.
factCheckIssues.fix: Removed the url from the GenAI provision. The 2019 URL stays in sources as the earlier circular.
factCheckIssues.evidence: The URL path contains 20191105-1-EN, which matches the 2019 circular. Search results report the GenAI circular around 19–21 Aug 2024.

factCheckIssues.problem: The 19 Aug 2024 date could not be confirmed: press coverage dates the circular around 21 Aug 2024. The customer 'options' (opt-out) expectation is only in secondary summaries.
factCheckIssues.fix: Kept the date at medium confidence and listed it in uncertain. Removed 'and their options'. Added the sandbox launch date (13 Aug 2024, confirmed by the info.gov.hk release) and the 2026 GenA.I. Sandbox++ expansion (March 2026 joint circular).
factCheckIssues.evidence: uabonline and cointelegraph coverage (21 Aug 2024); info.gov.hk P2024081300265 (HKMA and Cyberport launch GenA.I. Sandbox, 13 Aug 2024); MPFA joint circular 5 Mar 2026.

factCheckIssues.problem: The draft said the HKMA was the designated authority 'for operators it regulates' without saying what it administers. Under Cap. 653 the MA administers the Category 1 (organisational) and Category 2 (preventive) obligations for banking and financial services CIs. Category 3 incident notifications go to the Commissioner.
factCheckIssues.fix: Rewrote the summary to set out the three categories of duties, make the Commissioner the recipient of incident notifications, and limit the HKMA's role to the organisational and preventive obligations.
factCheckIssues.evidence: HKMA–Commissioner MoU (hkma.gov.hk Memorandum_of_Understanding.pdf, dated 29 May 2026) as quoted in search: the MA administers category 1 and category 2 obligations for banking and financial services CIs. Mayer Brown (Jan 2026) says designated authorities handle category 1 and 2.

factCheckIssues.problem: The draft did not mention the HKMA's own Cap. 653 Code of Practice for designated AIs. The MoU date was unconfirmed.
factCheckIssues.fix: Added the HKMA Code of Practice for AIs designated as CIOs (2 June 2026). Confirmed the MoU date of 29 May 2026 at medium confidence.
factCheckIssues.evidence: brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/current/20260527-25-EN (current issue date 02 Jun 2026, 'All Authorized Institutions'). hlc.com: HKMA codes for AIs, PSI operators and SVF licensees released 2–12 June 2026. Search excerpt of the MoU is dated 29 May 2026.

factCheckIssues.problem: The draft did not say who receives the Cap. 653 statutory notifications, so a reader could take the HKMA as the recipient.
factCheckIssues.fix: The text now says the statutory deadlines are for notifying the Commissioner. The itAngle point now refers to Cap. 653 clocks specifically.
factCheckIssues.evidence: Stephenson Harwood, Tanner De Witt and UPPERSETUP summaries: CIOs notify the Commissioner's Office of incidents within 12 or 48 hours, with a written report within 14 days.

factCheckIssues.problem: The draft left OR-2's status open, described the OR-1 revision only vaguely, linked the url to the cover letter instead of the module, and the counselNote contained 'seen in search results', which does not belong in learning material.
factCheckIssues.fix: Stated that OR-2 is a non-statutory guidance note and that the revised OR-1 is dated 25 July 2022. Changed the url to the OR-2 module PDF. The counselNote now names the June 2026 letter 'Operational Resilience: Sustaining and Uplifting'.
factCheckIssues.evidence: KPMG 2022 summary: OR-2 is a non-statutory guidance note, and revised OR-1 issued 25 July 2022. Deloitte: deadlines of 31 May 2023 and 31 May 2026. brdr OR-2 module URL 20220531-2-EN/OR-2.pdf. regalert and brdr 20260529-5 search summary: the June 2026 letter reports an HKMA survey finding that all AIs achieved resilience by end-May 2026.

factCheckIssues.problem: Only TM-G-1 was given as an example of a non-statutory module. OR-2 is also a non-statutory guidance note.
factCheckIssues.fix: Added OR-2 to the non-statutory examples.
factCheckIssues.evidence: KPMG summary of OR-2 status.

factCheckIssues.problem: The draft had TM-E-1 at medium confidence, although its version, date and statutory status can be confirmed. The 'ABC' measures were described too loosely.
factCheckIssues.fix: Added V.4 dated 25.10.24, its supersession of earlier non-statutory versions and of the 2016 internet banking security circular. Spelled out 'Authenticate in-App' (Q4 2025) and the August 2025 'ABCD' addition of deepfake detection. Raised confidence to high.
factCheckIssues.evidence: Search of HKMA TM-E-1 PDF and regulationtomorrow: statutory guideline under s.7(3), V.4 25.10.24, scope extended to payment cards, supersedes the 2016 circular. HKMA 20250411 and 20250825 documents and LCQ7 (7 May 2025): Authenticate in-App by Q4 2025, ABCD adds deepfake detection.

factCheckIssues.problem: The instrument title was generic. The draft said the circular requires 'management-endorsed internal criteria', which the available sources do not confirm.
factCheckIssues.fix: Corrected the title to 'Incident response and management procedures'. Recast the internal-criteria point as counsel's advice, based on the HKMA not having published a list of notifiable incidents. Added the 12 Aug 2014 circular that refers back to it.
factCheckIssues.evidence: centralbanking.com/risk.net headline 'HKMA issues incident response and management procedures'. LCQ15 (4 May 2011): notify the HKMA immediately. RPC: the HKMA has not listed notifiable incidents. regalert: the 12 Aug 2014 circular reminds AIs to observe the 22 Jun 2010 circular.

factCheckIssues.problem: Whether the guide supersedes the 2022 cloud guidance, and that guidance's exact title ('Guidance on Cloud Computing'), are confirmed only by secondary sources, and those sources name it differently.
factCheckIssues.fix: The text now says the guide 'is reported to supersede' the 2022 cloud guidance, without the exact title. Added the issue date of 8 Jan 2026 and the lifecycle approach, which are confirmed.
factCheckIssues.evidence: Search: HKMA letter of 8 January 2026, coverage expanded from four to eight domains, cloud is about 80% of reportable tech outsourcing. regalert and Thales disagree on the predecessor's name.

factCheckIssues.problem: The draft stated flatly that the 2.0 review 'added incident response and recovery practices'. Only one secondary source supports that wording.
factCheckIssues.fix: Reworded: the review streamlined the C-RAF assessment process and refreshed its control principles, with the incident response and recovery point attributed to industry summaries. Added the phased implementation.
factCheckIssues.evidence: HKMA press release 20201103-4 (via search): effective 1 Jan 2021, phased, three pillars unchanged. KPMG CFI 2.0 note: streamlined assessment.

factCheckIssues.problem: The draft expanded iCAST as 'intelligence-led attack simulation testing', which leaves out 'cyber'.
factCheckIssues.fix: Changed to 'intelligence-led cyber attack simulation testing (iCAST)'.
factCheckIssues.evidence: HKMA C-RAF terminology (Cyber Attack Simulation Testing).

factCheckIssues.problem: 'Agreements must give' overstates SA-2, which is a non-statutory guideline.
factCheckIssues.fix: Changed 'must give' to 'should give'.
factCheckIssues.evidence: SA-2 is a non-statutory SPM guidance module.

factCheckIssues.problem: 'Any SMS OTP fallback' did not reflect that the HKMA allows SMS OTP only in certain scenarios.
factCheckIssues.fix: Changed to 'any permitted SMS OTP fallback'.
factCheckIssues.evidence: HKMA 20250411 letter (via search): AIs may still allow SMS OTP in certain scenarios.

factCheckIssues.problem: The uncertain list did not reflect what was now verified, and several sources consulted were missing.
factCheckIssues.fix: Updated uncertain to show resolved points (OR-2 status, the ABC timeline, the MoU and CoP dates) and the points still open. Added the sources consulted.
factCheckIssues.evidence: See the searches above.

factCheckIssues.problem: The counselNote described s.72B as the approval provision for executive officers. According to the circular, executive officers are approved under s.71C, and s.72B relates to managers.
factCheckIssues.fix: Corrected the summary to list CEs and alternate CEs, s.71 directors, s.72B managers and s.71C executive officers. Revised the counselNote to match. Added the circular url. Recorded the s.71C/s.71D inconsistency in uncertain.
factCheckIssues.evidence: Search of HKMA circular 20171016 and Clifford Chance: 'management' covers CEs, alternate CEs, directors approved under s.71, s.72B managers and EOs approved under s.71C. A 2002 amending ordinance refers to s.71D.

factCheckIssues.problem: The draft said 'a chief executive of an AI was convicted of this in 2009'. The 30 Jan 2009 government release reports that two men were fined for Banking Ordinance offences, and the defendants' roles are unclear. The draft also did not mention that s.97 allows use of 'bank' with the MA's consent.
factCheckIssues.fix: Reworded to say the District Court fined individuals in January 2009 for offences including producing false information, and listed the details as uncertain. Added the MA-consent element to s.97 and the exceptions to s.92.
factCheckIssues.evidence: info.gov.hk P200901300305 'Two men fined for offences under Banking Ordinance' (via search). HKMA press release 20241115-3 on ss.97 and 97A. ICAC Bank on Integrity page lists ss.123 and 124.

factCheckIssues.problem: The ICAC press release index_id_1885 could not be linked to s.124 BO. ICAC search results showed POBO prosecutions, not s.124 charges.
factCheckIssues.fix: Replaced it with the ICAC Bank on Integrity page that describes ss.123 and 124. Added the other sources consulted.
factCheckIssues.evidence: hkbedc.icac.hk/bank/text/en/206.html lists BO s.124 (advantages for favour in granting credit) and s.123 (false entries).

factCheckIssues.problem: The claim that the CAMEL rating 'informs the capital it is expected to hold' could not be verified.
factCheckIssues.fix: Removed the clause. The rating is now said only to set supervisory intensity.
factCheckIssues.evidence: SA-1 search results confirm the integration with CAMEL and supervisory intensity, but say nothing about a capital link.

factCheckIssues.problem: The draft did not separate the notice power in s.59(2) from the MA's approval of the auditor in s.59(3).
factCheckIssues.fix: Changed the ref to s.59(2), (3) and explained both steps. Added the published examples (BOCHK 2003, Octopus Cards 2010).
factCheckIssues.evidence: HKMA press release 20100803-4: notice under s.59(2), approval of Deloitte under s.59(3). HKMA press release 20030611-3: s.59 report on BOCHK.

factCheckIssues.problem: The draft left out the s.23 procedure (notice of grounds and an opportunity to be heard), and the order of the suspension sections needed confirming.
factCheckIssues.fix: Added s.23. Confirmed s.24 (temporary suspension) and s.25 (suspension). Reworded the counselNote on revocation grounds to reflect the HKMA's statement that authorization criteria continue to apply.
factCheckIssues.evidence: LegCo LS70/04-05: revocation under s.22, suspension under s.25, temporary suspension under s.24. HKMA Guide to Authorization ch.5: s.22 on Eighth Schedule grounds, with s.23(1) notice and hearing.

factCheckIssues.problem: The draft did not identify the limbs of s.52 or give any practical examples.
factCheckIssues.fix: Added the limb references (A), (B) and (C), with examples: an Advisor direction for Octopus Cards Limited and a Manager for Delta Asia Credit Limited. The grounds remain at medium confidence.
factCheckIssues.evidence: HKMA press release 20090522-3 (revocation of the Octopus direction). info.gov.hk P200810240085 (revocation of the Delta Asia Credit Manager appointment). Search summary: s.52(1)(B) and (C) used in these cases.

factCheckIssues.problem: The description of s.63(2) needed support.
factCheckIssues.fix: Reworded to say s.63(2) supports further-information requests, citing the HKMA compliance certificate form, which gives s.63(2) as its legal basis. Kept at medium confidence.
factCheckIssues.evidence: HKMA form ma(bs)1fa: 'Information requested in this return is required under section 63(2) of the Banking Ordinance.'

factCheckIssues.problem: The draft did not name the eight inherent risks or mention the 2022 revision's treatment of emerging risks.
factCheckIssues.fix: Listed the eight risks and added that the 2022 revision expects emerging risks such as climate risk to be considered within them. V.2 date of 23 Dec 2022 confirmed.
factCheckIssues.evidence: brdr SA-1 V.2 (20221223) and V.1 (20011011) via search. Linklaters note on the 2022 revision and emerging risks.

factCheckIssues.problem: The Advisor definition did not say that the MA appoints the Advisor and that the institution is required to seek its advice. The tribunal entry said 'hears appeals' and did not mention its origin.
factCheckIssues.fix: Redefined Advisor as an MA-appointed person whose advice the institution must seek under s.52. For the tribunal, used 'reviews' and added that it was originally the Capital Adequacy Review Tribunal. Chair qualification confirmed.
factCheckIssues.evidence: LegCo bc050602cb1-1670: chairman qualified for appointment as a High Court judge under s.9 of Cap. 4. Ord. 3 of 2012 broadened the functions of the Capital Adequacy Review Tribunal. info.gov.hk 2024 release on BRT chairman appointment.

factCheckIssues.problem: The uncertain list needed updating: some points were resolved and new ones had emerged (s.71C/s.71D, the 2009 case details, the dates of the s.52 examples).
factCheckIssues.fix: Updated the uncertain list.
factCheckIssues.evidence: See the searches above. Legal Data Hunter could not be used because the daily quota was reached, so statute text was not checked directly.
